skill.name: airtable-automation
skill.description: Automate Airtable record, schema, and comment workflows through the Composio toolkit on Rube MCP.
skill.summary: Manage Airtable records and schemas with schema-aware Rube MCP workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 55 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting, with no shell or Ruby execution present. The external MCP connection is real, and destructive Airtable operations lack an explicit confirmation safeguard.

remediation.issue: Record deletion and schema changes can cause irreversible or disruptive workspace changes without a required confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preview and explicit user confirmation before deletions, bulk updates, field changes, or table metadata changes.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends Airtable requests through the external Rube MCP and Composio service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the third-party data path and recommend least-privilege Airtable access before authentication.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Airtable connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `airtable`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `tableIdOrName`: Table ID (starts with 'tbl') or table name
- `fields`: Object mapping field names to values
- `typecast`: Set true for automatic type conversion
- `fields`: Array of field names to return
- `maxRecords`: Max total records across all pages
- Field names in formulas must be wrapped in `{}` and match schema exactly
- String values must be quoted: `{Status}='Active'` not `{Status}=Active`
- `options`: Type-specific options (choices for select, precision for number)
- Single quotes in values: double them (`{Name}='John''s Company'`)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

content.value_statement: Airtable operations often fail when field names, formulas, limits, or pagination are handled incorrectly. This skill provides schema-aware workflows through Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Discovers available Airtable bases and inspects table schemas before operations.
Lists and filters records with formulas, selected fields, sorting, limits, and pagination.
Creates, updates, and deletes individual records or batches of up to ten records.
Creates fields, updates field names or descriptions, and changes table metadata.
Lists comments attached to an Airtable record.
Handles common Airtable errors, identifier formats, rate limits, and pagination rules.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP, Composio, and an active authenticated Airtable connection.
Batch record operations support at most ten records per request, while list pages support at most 100 records.
Computed fields cannot be created, and existing field types or options cannot be changed.
The documented comment workflow lists comments but does not add, edit, or delete them.

use_cases.title: Maintain Operations Records
use_cases.description: Create and update task, inventory, or request records while respecting Airtable schemas and batch limits.

use_cases.title: Query Structured Data
use_cases.description: Filter records with Airtable formulas, selected fields, sorting, and stable pagination.

use_cases.title: Evolve Workspace Schema
use_cases.description: Inspect tables, create fields, rename fields, and update table metadata with validated parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Base
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Airtable bases. Inspect the schema for [base and table], then summarize each field name, type, and purpose.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with read-only discovery before planning changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find Matching Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Find records in [base and table] where [conditions]. Return [fields], sort by [field], and continue through every page.
prompt_templates.scenario: Query records with a validated Airtable formula.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Batch Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview records matching [conditions]. After I confirm, update [fields] in batches of ten and report successes and failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify a controlled record set with confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Field Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my schema and plan a safe migration from [old field] to [new field]. Migrate in batches, validate totals, and preserve the original.
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle a schema change that requires replacement and data migration.

output_examples.input: Show active customer records and return only the name, owner, and renewal date.
output: Matched 42 active customer records across one table.
Returned the requested fields and followed all pagination offsets.

output_examples.input: Create follow-up records for 23 approved requests.
output: Validated the destination schema and required fields.
Prepared three batches containing 10, 10, and 3 records.
Created 23 records and reported their Airtable record identifiers.

output_examples.input: Rename the Priority field to Urgency.
output_examples.output: Confirmed the current field identifier, previewed the rename, and updated the field name after approval. The field type and options remained unchanged.

best_practices: Inspect the current base schema before building formulas or sending record fields.
Preview affected records and obtain explicit confirmation before destructive or structural changes.
Keep filters, sorting, and views unchanged while following pagination offsets.
anti_patterns: Do not guess base, table, field, or record identifiers.
Do not send more than ten records in one create, update, or delete request.
Do not reuse an offset after changing filters, sorting, or views.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to Airtable?
faq.answer: No. It uses the Composio Airtable toolkit through Rube MCP and requires an authenticated Airtable connection.

faq.question: Can it create bases or tables?
faq.answer: No documented workflow creates bases or tables. It can inspect bases, update table metadata, and create fields.

faq.question: Can it process large record sets?
faq.answer: Yes, with pagination and batches. Writes use groups of ten, and list pages contain at most 100 records.

faq.question: Does it support Airtable comments?
faq.answer: It documents listing comments only. Adding, editing, or deleting comments is not included.

faq.question: How should destructive changes be handled?
faq.answer: Inspect the schema, preview affected records, and confirm deletions or schema changes before execution.

faq.question: Can it build Airtable filter formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers comparisons, logical functions, text search, date checks, field syntax, and quote escaping.
